Cc: Peter Zhang <p.zhang@acme.com>, Lina Torres <lina.torres@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft: customer-facing root cause recap + remediation plan (attached)

Hi all — attaching a customer-facing draft RCA and a compact timeline CSV. Below is an executive summary intended for Acme leadership; please review and flag anything you want reworded before I drop the final PDF to Peter.

Executive summary (for customers)
- What happened: Between 13:45 and 14:22 PDT on Sep 12, some requests to Acme's primary inference route experienced increased tail latency and intermittent timeouts. Impact: ~8% of requests exceeded the 2.5s SLO; error rate rose to ~1.8% during the window.
- Root cause: a race condition in the serving autoscaler coupled with an KV-cache invalidation bug. During a transient CPU scheduling spike on one serving pool, the autoscaler launched replacement workers while the cache invalidation process for model shards retried; under load the cache population path failed to populate the local KV cache for a subset of shards, leading to repeated cold-cache penalties on a portion of shard requests.
- Why this wasn’t prevented: the autoscaler health checks did not surface the specific cache-population failure; our internal integration tests did not simulate the exact combination of CPU scheduling spike + sustained request fanout that occurred during your peak.

Timeline (abridged)
- 13:45 PDT: latency increases begin; alert triggers for elevated 95/99 latency on route acme-checkout-primary.
- 13:47 PDT: Acme SRE reports timeouts to Redwood support (trace bundle received).
- 13:50–14:05 PDT: on-call begins triage; autoscaler activity observed; engineers reproduce cache-miss pattern in staging.
- 14:10 PDT: mitigation applied — temporary route pinning to warm pool and disabling autoscaler bursts for the route.
- 14:22 PDT: tail latency returns to baseline for pinned route; overall error rate normalizes.

Immediate and medium-term actions (customer-facing commitments)
1) Rollout bug fix (code): patch to the cache invalidation + backoff logic; target: v1.2.3 rollout to hosted by Sep 20, owner: Markus K.
2) Autoscaler safety net: add a cache-population health check and a fail-open for autoscaler bursts; target: Sep 27, owner: Marissa C.
3) Hardening tests: new e2e scenario that simulates CPU pressure + high fanout; target: Sep 24, owner: Reliability Eng QA team (cc'd).
4) Operational safety: add a per-route pin-and-warm runbook and 1-click rollback for high-impact customers; immediate runbook available now, automation scheduled by Sep 30.
5) Compensation: one month of free premium token credits applied to Acme account for measurable impact; details to be confirmed by your account team.

Attachments: acme-rca-draft-20260913.pdf (PDF) — customer-facing one-page summary
incident-timeline-20260913.csv (CSV) — detailed timestamped events and metrics

Please review — Vanessa, if this language looks good I will export to PDF and send to Peter with the attachments.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Incident Response, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Draft: customer-facing root cause recap + remediation plan (attached)

Markus — thanks for the clear summary. The technical explanation maps to the traces we saw. A few quick asks:
- Please add the exact Model IDs affected in the final summary (acme-model-v3, acme-model-v3-aux).
- Can you add a short note on monitoring thresholds we'll get notified on if this recurs?

The proposed timeline is reasonable. We'd like weekly status emails until the autoscaler safety net is deployed. If you can send the PDF and timeline CSV and a HubSpot ticket ID, we'll mark this as resolved on our side pending the fix rollout updates.

Thanks,
Peter
